A retrieval system can read the values but cannot say what any of them is a value OF, so it will either decline to quote the table or attach a number to the wrong label. suggested_action.mechanism: Extractors bind a cell to its column through the header row; with no <th>, scope or caption there is no machine-readable link between a value and its meaning, so the fact cannot be quoted with the label that makes it true.

findings.evidence: On https://www.npr.org/: the homepage declares ['speakablespecification'] and none of it is an Organization, LocalBusiness or Person node, so nothing states who runs this site.

suggested_action.mechanism: A named, linked entity lets a consumer connect statements on this site to the same entity elsewhere; without it the brand is an unlinked string that may collide with other things sharing the name.
suggested_action.patch:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Organization",
  "@id": "https://www.npr.org/#organization",
  "name": "NPR - Breaking News, Analysis, Music, Arts & Podcasts : NPR",
  "url": "https://www.npr.org/",
  "description": "Top stories in the U.S. and world news, politics, health, science, business, music, arts and culture. Nonprofit journalism with a mission. This is NPR.",
  "sameAs": [
    "__FILL_IN__:your_wikipedia_or_wikidata_url",
    "__FILL_IN__:your_linkedin_url",
    "__FILL_IN__:your_primary_social_or_github_url"
  ]
}
</script>
suggested_action.source: schema.org/Organization; handout appendix, Why agreement across the web matters
suggested_action.summary: Publish an Organization node on the homepage with sameAs links to your real profiles.
suggested_action.verification: curl -s https://www.npr.org/ | grep -o '"sameAs"[^]]*]'

findings.title: The sitemap does not usefully describe the site

findings.evidence: This is a site-wide pattern, not a one-page defect: it appears on 24 of 25 crawled pages (96%), so it is almost certainly emitted by a shared template and fixable in one place. Reported once rather than 24 times. Example: https://www.npr.org/: no H1; heading levels skip from h4 to h6. Outline: h2:'Health Reporting in the States', h2:'Health', h2:'Weather', h2:'Technology', h2:'Only on NPR', h2:'Business', h2:'National', h2:'Deep Dive'. Headings are where a reader decides which part of a page answers the question, so an outline that does not divide the content leaves it to guess.

suggested_action.mechanism: Headings mark the boundaries a reader uses to locate the relevant part of a long page; without them the whole page is one undifferentiated block.
suggested_action.patch:
__FILL_IN__:page_subject

__FILL_IN__:question_this_section_answers
suggested_action.summary: Give the page one H1 and H2 sections that name what each part answers.
suggested_action.verification: curl -s https://www.npr.org/ | grep -oE '<h[1-3][^>]*>' | sort | uniq -c

limitations.confidence_effect: not assessed; re-run with --probe-bot-ua to close this gap
limitations.reason:
Edge and CDN reachability for named AI crawlers was not assessed, because --probe-bot-ua was not set. This is the highest-value check in this marketplace: a CDN or WAF rule that returns 403 to OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot or Claude-SearchBot removes a brand from those assistants entirely, and leaves no trace in robots.txt or in what a human sees. If you own this site, re-run the orchestrator with the --probe-bot-ua flag:
    orchestrate.py <url> --out ./audit-output --probe-bot-ua
That sends ONE request per crawler, to the homepage only, with an auditor token appended to the user-agent string so it is identifiable in your logs. It is off by default because sending named-crawler user-agents to a site you do not own is not something an audit should do without being asked.
